clue.text: Co graduate blocking youth

indicators.note: the graduate sits in the way of the youth, stopping it up from inside

parts.note: a colt is a young, inexperienced person, from the young horse
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate's degree

explanation.surface: A company graduate gets in the way of a young recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Co' looks like company, but it is the chemical symbol of the element being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Co is the chemical symbol for this metallic element, so the symbol stands for its name.

clue.text: Fortune concealed in church linen

indicators.note: concealed in puts the fortune inside the church

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or fate

explanation.surface: Wealth hidden away among a church's altar linens.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a woven fabric, so it is a type of material or textile.

clue.text: My God! Daughter goes up taken in by curse for bed-time ghoulie

indicators.note: taken in by means the piece is held inside the curse

parts.note: a ban is an old word for a curse

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the remaining letters from bottom to top
the daughter goes, leaving the exclamation without that letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A child's frightened exclamation as she goes upstairs, cursing the bedtime monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My God!' reads as a child's cry, but it is fodder: the daughter must leave before the rest turns upward, or the letters come out wrong. BAN as curse is an archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogeyman is an imaginary monster used to frighten children at bedtime, a kind of ghoul.

clue.text: What must be penned exists to vacuous clerk

parts.note: to exist is to live, so exists gives lives
taken as written

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so only the first and last letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: Something that has to be written out for an empty-headed office worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' suggests writing, but it means kept in pens.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm animals are kept in pens, so they are what must be penned.

clue.text: Set limit on country with name forgotten

indicators.note: a forgotten piece is left out, so the name's letter drops from the country

parts.note: Denmark is a Scandinavian country

explanation.surface: A nation that forgets its own name sets a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: To demark is to fix a boundary or limit, a variant spelling of demarcate.

clue.text: Lamb-like I'll enter windy lane

indicators.note: enter means the letter goes inside the rearranged lane
a windy lane twists, so its letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: I'll reads as I will, so the letter I is what will enter

explanation.surface: A young sheep says it will go into a winding country road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windy' turns LANE into ELAN, and 'enter' puts I inside. Charles Lamb wrote as Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb wrote his essays under the pen name Elia, so the adjective means in his style.

clue.text: White record on extremes of emotion

parts.note: an album is a long-playing record

indicators.note: extremes of means the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A white record of feelings at their most intense.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is egg white, the clear part that turns white when cooked.

clue.text: How thousands of cycles are rated?

definitions.text: How thousands of cycles are rated?

parts.words: How thousands of cycles are rated?
parts.note: frequency is measured in cycles per second, a thousand of them forming one larger unit

explanation.surface: How bicycles are graded in their thousands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycles' suggests bicycles; it means oscillations per second.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit equals one thousand cycles per second, used for rating radio frequencies.

clue.text: Act mercifully towards small organisation among a handful?

indicators.note: among says the short organisation sits within the handful

parts.note: a hand has five fingers, so a handful is five
org is the shortened form of organisation

explanation.surface: Show mercy to a small outfit that is lost among a handful of people.
explanation.walkthrough: A handful as five comes from the five fingers of a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To pardon someone is to act mercifully towards them, letting an offence go.

clue.text: Motley dish with nothing on top

parts.note: a pie is a baked dish
a bald head has no hair on top

explanation.surface: A colourful meal served with no crust on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald horse has patches of two colours, so it is motley or variegated in colouring.

clue.text: Episode from sit-com put in global reckoning

indicators.note: an episode is a segment, so a run of letters is taken out of these words

explanation.surface: An instalment of a television comedy shown worldwide.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckoning is calculating, and computing is the act of working out figures.

clue.text: This digital signal could be a bad sign

definitions.text: This digital signal could be a bad sign

parts.words: This digital signal could be a bad sign
parts.note: digital means made with the fingers and thumbs, so this is a hand gesture meaning disapproval

explanation.surface: A computer signal might be an ill omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests electronics; here it means done with the digits of the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The gesture of turned-down thumbs signals rejection, which is a bad sign for whoever receives it.

clue.text: Initially measures objects' hardness somehow

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: A rough way of gauging how hard things are.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohs scale is the standard scale of mineral hardness, measuring how hard objects are by scratch tests.

clue.text: Something to pluck found on your knee, Susanna

definitions.text: Something to pluck found on your knee, Susanna

parts.words: Something to pluck found on your knee, Susanna
parts.note: the song Oh! Susanna has a singer coming with a stringed instrument on his knee

explanation.surface: A line from a folk song addressed to a girl named Susanna.
explanation.walkthrough: The American song Oh! Susanna begins 'I come from Alabama with a ... on my knee'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a stringed instrument played by plucking, famous from the Stephen Foster song.

clue.text: Sam Browne's belt, black and more slippery dropped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dropped means a letter falls out, here the I

parts.note: oilier means greasier and so more slippery

explanation.surface: A soldier's black belt has grown greasier and fallen down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes I from OILIER to leave OLIER; the clue does not name the letter, a loose touch. A Sam Browne is an officer's belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolier is a shoulder belt for ammunition, like the Sam Browne belt with its cross-strap.

clue.text: Darn type exploding this misplaced learning

indicators.note: an exploding word is blown apart and its letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A frustrated cry at a kind of fussy scholarship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploding' scatters DARNTYPE into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive or misplaced show of learning, fussing over trivial points of scholarship.

clue.text: Cameron for example, led us astray first having no defined plan

indicators.note: first places the rearranged letters before the party member
astray means gone wrong, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
David Cameron was a Conservative prime minister, a Tory

explanation.surface: A political leader steered the country wrongly with no clear plan.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron was a British prime minister who led the Conservative (Tory) party; the surface makes him the one who led us astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Desultory means aimless and unmethodical, lacking a plan or purpose.

clue.text: Potted cabbage or mint?

definitions.meaning: in snooker a potted ball has gone into a pocket
cabbage is slang for banknotes and making a mint is earning lots, so this is having gained money

explanation.surface: Something sounding like a list of vegetables and herbs in pots.
explanation.walkthrough: Cabbage and mint look like garden plants for a pot, but both are slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a ball sunk is in a pocket; a person who has made money on a deal is said to be ahead financially.

clue.text: Cook to carve ham

indicators.note: to cook something is to falsify or rework it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing and slicing a joint of ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges TOCARVE. 'Ham' is the definition as a verb, to act badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform with exaggeration, the same as to exaggerate a role on stage.

clue.text: Take a quick look at son with pump

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them closely, as does a quiz

explanation.surface: Glance at your son while he works a pump.
explanation.walkthrough: SQUIZ is Australian and British slang for a quick look; the clue uses it as a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A squiz is slang for a brief glance, so having one means taking a quick look.

clue.text: Let go, let go donkey, you said first

indicators.note: first places the letter before the rearranged animal

parts.note: the word you spoken sounds like the letter U

indicators.note: letting go of something releases it to fall apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone told to release a donkey says it was you who did it first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let go' appears twice: first as the definition, then as the signal rearranging DONKEY to NYOKED; 'you said' gives U, put 'first'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unyoke an animal is to free it from its harness, so the past form means released.

clue.text: An architectural element which could be funny?

definitions.text: An architectural element which could be funny?

parts.words: An architectural element which could be funny?
parts.note: a structural part of the body's framework, and one kind is named after a sensitive spot on the elbow

explanation.surface: A building feature that might make you laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: The skeleton is the body's architecture; the funny one is the nerve point at the elbow.
explanation.definitionFit: Bones form the structural framework of the body, and the funny one is the elbow's sensitive spot.

clue.text: Expat nobly fixed up a rink-side seat for minors or majors?

definitions.text: a rink-side seat for minors or majors?

indicators.note: fixed up means put together anew, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An aristocratic emigrant gets a good seat beside an ice rink for children or army officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed up' rearranges EXPATNOBLY. In ice hockey, minors and majors are penalties, not young people or army ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: In ice hockey, a player given a minor or major penalty sits in the box beside the rink.

clue.text: Power changing only if this drops

definitions.text: Power changing only if this drops

indicators.note: changing means the letters of the next word alter their order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The electricity supply only changes when this falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a fallen power mast cuts or changes the supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon carries power lines, so if one falls the electricity supply is interrupted.

clue.text: The sort of nerve needed to see where spirits come from

definitions.text: The sort of nerve needed to see
definitions.meaning: the nerve carrying signals from eye to brain is named for sight
in a pub, spirits are dispensed through a measuring device fixed to an upturned bottle

explanation.surface: Courage is needed to look at the source of ghosts.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs, spirits are poured through a measured dispenser fitted to the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: The optic nerve serves sight, and an optic is a pub's measure for spirits.

clue.text: Vehicle reversing a long way around that, it's amazing!

indicators.note: around has the long distance wrapping the turned vehicle

parts.note: a mile is a long way

indicators.note: reversing reads the vehicle's word backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car backing up over a long distance would be astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is only a link; the exclamation 'it's amazing!' is the definition, naming a wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amazing beyond explanation is a marvel or wonder, the sense of the exclamation.

clue.text: Chinese toy with black neat hawk

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a kite is a bird of prey of the hawk family

explanation.surface: A Chinese plaything with a tidy black bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' as cattle is an old word that crosswords keep alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Box kites are flying toys, and kites in general originated in China.

clue.text: Plump fish endlessly caught by cane

indicators.note: caught by puts the shortened fish inside the cane

parts.note: a rod is a cane or stick

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: A fat fish keeps being hooked by an angler's cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' could be a verb (choose), but here it is the adjective meaning fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund means round and plump in figure, a synonym for chubby.

clue.text: Small dictionary on synonym for "old judge"

indicators.note: on puts the dictionary piece after the synonym piece in the across entry

parts.note: syn is the short form of synonym
small signals shortening, dic being a brief form of dictionary

explanation.surface: A pocket thesaurus entry offers another word for an ancient magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: Dictionary is usually shortened to dict; here it is cut to DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndic was a magistrate or judge in ancient Greece, later a civic officer elsewhere.
